Serie A Guide

Published 5 September 2026 Serie A TV96 Live Editorial Team Evergreen guide · 4 min read
Back to News & Guides

Serie A is Italy's top men's football division. Its championship is often called the Scudetto, a term associated with the shield worn by the champions. Following the league means tracking a long points race while recognising that Italian ranking rules can treat certain decisive ties differently from the rules familiar in other countries.

This guide explains the competition's structure and offers a practical way to read its matches. It avoids assuming that every Italian team plays one style or that historical reputation determines a current season.

A home-and-away league season

Serie A has 20 clubs, each playing the other 19 at home and away. That produces 38 league fixtures per team. Victories earn three points, draws one and defeats none. The accumulated table identifies the championship race, European contenders and clubs threatened by relegation.

The Coppa Italia is separate. A cup victory can be important for a club's season and European prospects, but it does not add points to its Serie A total. Keep competition labels visible when evaluating a sequence of results across several tournaments.

How to approach equal points

Italian table rules use head-to-head comparisons in ordinary tied-position situations, but special play-off provisions can apply when the championship or the final relegation boundary is tied. A general data table should not be treated as the final authority on those exceptional outcomes.

For example, two invented clubs might appear next to each other on equal points, separated by the displayed goal difference. If that equality concerns the decisive safety position, the correct question is whether the current regulations require a play-off, not simply which GD number is larger.

Multiple-team ties can require an additional procedure to identify the relevant clubs. Check the applicable season's regulations and league announcement before describing a tied club as champion, safe or relegated. The goal difference guide explains why a familiar statistic is not always the decisive rule.

Europe and the second division

High finishes provide routes to UEFA competitions according to Italy's allocation. Domestic cup winners, additional European Performance Spots and title-holder arrangements can alter the final picture. There is no reason to assume one season's exact boundary will remain fixed forever.

Three clubs leave Serie A for Serie B at the end of the campaign, subject to the rules resolving the final order. Promotion replaces them with clubs from the second tier. The survival race therefore concerns a real change in the club's next competitive programme.

European qualification and domestic survival are separate questions even when a cup run overlaps with a difficult league season. Track each route independently rather than assuming one achievement automatically resolves the other.

A little historical context

The unified national league format began in 1929/30. Italian football's major clubs have built rivalries over many generations, and the competition has repeatedly attracted players and coaches from around the world. That history helps explain the expectations surrounding the Scudetto.

It should not become a shortcut for describing today's football. A league containing different squads, budgets and coaching approaches cannot be reduced to a single defensive stereotype. The useful question is what a particular team is doing in the match in front of you.

Reading tactical shape

Formation graphics describe starting positions imperfectly. A team shown with three centre-backs may defend with five players across the back when its wing-backs retreat. In possession, one of those defenders may move forward to help create an extra passing option.

Watch where the spare player appears. If an opponent presses with two forwards against three defenders, the defenders may initially have an extra player. The next question is whether they can use that advantage to find a midfielder, or whether the opponent blocks the central passing lanes.

Also observe what happens when a forward drops towards the ball. If a defender follows, space may open behind. If the defender stays, the forward may receive between the lines. This is a more specific way to explain a tactical contest than calling one side clever and the other passive.

Making a fair performance comparison

Compare league results with league results before adding cup performances. Then account for games played and home-away balance. A team with two matches in hand has opportunities remaining, but the table has not yet awarded it their points.

When discussing defensive strength, consider both goals conceded and the chances allowed. A clean sheet can follow strong control or excellent goalkeeping under pressure. If using xG, name the source and avoid implying that TV96 Live supplies that metric when it is absent from the data.

Using the site during a Serie A round

Choose Serie A on Standings and consult Matches for available fixtures and results. Recheck the table after completed matches have been incorporated, particularly when several clubs are close together.

Use the official league source to settle exceptional tied positions. For the European side of the season, our Champions League qualification guide explains the distinction between domestic ranking, allocated places and entry stages. Together, these checks make a table position more informative without asking it to explain everything.
